hook.convey: two same-size wholes, one cut into 4 equal parts, the other into 8 → 8 is the bigger number, yet each of its parts is smaller → which single part to pick is the question

use.hi: Socho, do bilkul ek jaisi roti. Ek ke 4 barabar hisse kiye, doosri ke 8. Aaj dekhenge ki kis roti ka ek hissa bada hota hai.
use.en: Picture two rotis, exactly alike. One is cut into 4 equal parts, the other into 8. Today we see which roti's single part is bigger.

use.hi: Socho, colour karne ke liye kaagaz ki do bilkul ek jaisi patti. Ek ko 4 barabar hisson mein baanto, doosri ko 8 mein. Aaj dekhenge ki kis patti ka ek hissa bada hota hai.
use.en: Picture two paper strips for colouring, exactly alike. Split one into 4 equal parts, the other into 8. Today we see which strip's single part is bigger.

explain.convey: one bar = one whole; 4 equal parts; 1 shaded part = 1/4; bottom number = how many equal parts the whole is cut into → predict: more cuts of the same bar, one part smaller

viewCaption.hi: Yeh wahi poora hai, bas patti ki jagah gol: chaar barabar hisse, aur ek mein rang.
viewCaption.en: This is the same whole, as a circle instead of a strip: four equal parts, and one is coloured.

prompt.hi: Is patti mein kitne barabar hisse hain?
prompt.en: How many equal parts does this strip have?

say.hi: Is patti mein 4 barabar hisse hain.

point.hi: Yeh patti ek poora hai: 4 barabar hisse, aur ek mein rang bhara hai. Woh ek hissa 1/4 hai. 1/4 ka 4 batata hai ki patti ke 4 barabar hisse hain.
point.en: This strip is one whole: 4 equal parts, and one is coloured in. That one part is 1/4. The 4 of 1/4 says the strip has 4 equal parts.

pointAlt.hi: Ek roti 4 bachche barabar baantein, toh har bachche ko roti ka 1/4 milta hai. Is patti ka rang wala hissa bhi waisa hi hai: chaar barabar mein se ek.
pointAlt.en: If 4 children share a roti equally, each child gets 1/4 of the roti. The coloured part of this strip is just like that: one of four equal parts.

prompt.hi: Doosri patti usi lambai ki hai, par 8 barabar hisson mein kati hai. Iska ek hissa pehli patti ke ek hisse se bada hai ya chhota?
prompt.en: The second strip is the same length, but cut into 8 equal parts. Is one part of it bigger or smaller than one part of the first strip?

reask.hi: Doosri patti ka ek hissa, pehli patti ke ek hisse se bada hai ya chhota?
reask.en: Is one part of the second strip bigger or smaller than one part of the first strip?

accept: smaller than the first strip's part

why.hi: dono patti barabar lambi hain, par doosri 8 hisson mein kati hai aur pehli sirf 4 mein
why.en: both strips are equally long, but the second is cut into 8 parts and the first into only 4

whyShort.hi: doosri patti 8 hisson mein kati, pehli sirf 4 mein
whyShort.en: the second is in 8 parts, the first in 4

whyAlt.hi: Ek hi patti ko 4 log baantein ya 8 log: 8 logon mein baantne par kisi ke haath utna nahi aata jitna 4 logon mein baantne par.
whyAlt.en: Share one strip among 4 people or among 8: shared among 8, nobody gets as much as when 4 share it.

simpler.hi: Pehli patti ke rangin hisse ke theek neeche dekho, aur doosri patti ke jo hisse us jagah mein aate hain, unhe gino.
simpler.en: Look right under the first strip's coloured part, and count the second strip's parts that fit in that space.

viewCaption.hi: Yahan dono patti ki jagah 0 se 1 tak ek number line hai: line ke upar 4 barabar gap, line ke neeche 8, aur line ke upar pehle gap ke ant par ek mark hai. Mark tak ka gap aur line ke neeche ka pehla gap, dono zero se hi shuru hote hain.
viewCaption.en: Here the two strips become one number line from 0 to 1: 4 equal gaps above the line, 8 below it, and a mark at the end of the first gap above the line. The gap up to the mark and the first gap below the line both start right at zero.

simpler.hi: Rang wala hissa chaar baar ek ke baad ek lagao, toh poori patti ban jaati hai. Isliye woh patti ka 1/4 hai.
simpler.en: Lay the coloured part end to end four times and you get the whole strip. That is why it is 1/4 of the strip.

explain.convey: same-size bar now in 8 equal parts → 1 part = 1/8 → the bars lie one under the other, so two lower parts line up under one top part → which top fraction do two 1/8 parts make

viewCaption.hi: Is gol ko aath barabar hisson mein kaata gaya hai, aur rang sirf ek hisse mein hai.
viewCaption.en: This circle is cut into eight equal parts, with colour in just one of them.

prompt.hi: Is patti ka ek hissa kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: What fraction is one part of this strip?

say.hi: Is patti ka ek hissa 1/8 hai.
say.en: One part of this strip is 1/8.

point.hi: Yeh wahi patti hai jo abhi dekhi: 8 barabar hisse, toh ek hissa 1/8. Dono patti ek hi jagah shuru aur khatam hoti hain, toh inhe seedha milaa sakte ho.
point.en: This is the same strip you just saw: 8 equal parts, so one part is 1/8. Both strips start and end at the same place, so you can match them straight.

pointAlt.hi: Ek kaagaz ki patti ko aadha modo, phir aadha, phir aadha: kholne par 8 barabar hisse milte hain, aur har hissa 1/8 hai.
pointAlt.en: Fold a paper strip in half, then in half, then in half again: when you open it there are 8 equal parts, and each part is 1/8.

prompt.hi: Doosri patti ke pehle do 1/8 hisse jodo. Woh milkar pehli patti ka kaunsa fraction banate hain?
prompt.en: Join the first two 1/8 parts of the second strip. Together, what fraction of the first strip do they make?

reask.hi: Doosri patti ke pehle do 1/8 hisse milkar pehli patti ka kaunsa fraction banate hain?
reask.en: What fraction of the first strip do the second strip's first two 1/8 parts make together?

why.hi: 8 hisson wali patti ke do 1/8 hisse milkar 4 hisson wali patti ka ek hissa, yaani 1/4, banate hain
why.en: two 1/8 parts of the 8-part strip together make one part of the 4-part strip, that is 1/4

whyShort.hi: do 1/8 hisse milkar ek 1/4 hissa banate hain
whyShort.en: two 1/8 parts together make one 1/4 part

whyAlt.hi: Pehli patti ke ek hisse ko beech se aadha kaato, toh do chhote hisse bante hain, har ek doosri patti ke ek hisse jitna.
whyAlt.en: Cut one part of the first strip down the middle and you get two small parts, each as long as one part of the second strip.

simpler.hi: Do 1/8 hisson ka sira dekho, aur dekho pehli patti mein usi jagah tak kaunsa hissa khatam hota hai.
simpler.en: Look where the two 1/8 parts end, and see which part of the first strip ends at that same spot.

viewCaption.hi: Yahan do ek jaise gol hain, ek 4 barabar hisson mein aur doosra 8 mein. 8 wale gol ke do saath wale hisse dekho, aur dono gol ko saath rakh kar milao.
viewCaption.en: Here are two identical circles, one in 4 equal parts and the other in 8. Look at two neighbouring parts of the 8-circle, and set the two circles side by side.

simpler.hi: 8 dost ek patti barabar baantein, toh har dost ko 1/8 milta hai. Pehli patti bhi utni hi lambi thi, isliye dono ko ek ke neeche ek rakh kar milaa sakte ho.
simpler.en: If 8 friends share one strip equally, each friend gets 1/8. The first strip was just as long, so you can lay the two one under the other and match them.

explain.convey: one 0-to-1 line, thirds above and sevenths below → further from 0 = bigger; by that rule 1/8 < 1/4 → which of 1/3, 1/7 stops further from 0

viewCaption.en: Here the same line becomes two strips: the first strip in three equal parts, the second in seven, both equally long from 0 to 1.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche kitne barabar gap hain?
prompt.en: How many equal gaps are below the line?

say.hi: Line ke neeche 7 barabar gap hain.
say.en: There are 7 equal gaps below the line.

point.hi: Patti mein dekha tha ki 1/8 chhota hai. Number line par chhota fraction zero ke zyada paas rukta hai, kyunki line par zero se jitna door, utna bada. Is line par, 0 se 1 tak, upar 3 barabar gap hain aur neeche 7.
point.en: With the strips we saw that 1/8 is smaller. On a number line the smaller fraction stops nearer zero, because the farther from zero, the bigger. On this line, from 0 to 1, there are 3 equal gaps on top and 7 below.

pointAlt.hi: Line ko ek ruler socho: 0 cm se jitna aage mark, utni lambi cheez. Isi tarah line par jo fraction zero se jitna aage ruke, woh utna bada.
pointAlt.en: Think of the line as a ruler: the farther the mark from 0 cm, the longer the thing. In the same way, the farther from zero a fraction stops on the line, the bigger it is.

prompt.hi: Isi line par, zero se zyada door kaun rukega, 1/3 ya 1/7?
prompt.en: On this line, which one stops further from zero, 1/3 or 1/7?

why.hi: 1/3 ka gap 1/7 ke gap se bada hai, toh 1/3 zero se aage jaakar rukta hai
why.en: a 1/3 gap is bigger than a 1/7 gap, so 1/3 stops further from zero

whyShort.hi: 1/3 ka gap bada, toh woh aage rukta hai
whyShort.en: a 1/3 gap is bigger, so it stops further

whyAlt.hi: 0 se 1 tak ki line sirf 3 gap mein bati ho toh har gap bada hota hai, 7 gap mein bati ho toh har gap chhota, aur pehla mark ek gap ke baad hi aata hai.
whyAlt.en: If the line from 0 to 1 is cut into only 3 gaps, each gap is big; in 7 gaps each is small, and the first mark comes just one gap along.

simpler.hi: Dono taraf ka pehla gap dekho, aur socho jis taraf gap kam hain, wahan har gap kitna lamba hoga.
simpler.en: Look at the first gap on each side, and think how long each gap must be on the side with fewer gaps.

viewCaption.hi: Dono patti ka pehla hissa 0 se shuru hota hai, ek teen hisson wali patti mein aur ek saat hisson wali mein.

simpler.hi: Do cheentiyan 0 se chalti hain: jo kam door pahunchi, uski doori chhoti. Line par bhi jo fraction pehle ruke, woh chhota.
simpler.en: Two ants set off from 0: the one that got less far went the shorter distance. On the line too, the fraction that stops first is the smaller.
